skills.name: engineering-review
skills.purpose: Review-only holistic engineering/code review of backend and frontend changes producing findings and a PASS/CHANGES-REQUESTED verdict, including Spec Kit compliance and delegated test-code review.
skills.trigger: Fires whenever the user asks to review code, a diff, a PR, a branch, or a change, or shares freshly implemented code for a quality/architecture check — "even if they don't say the word review"; also on Spec Kit markers (Phase, US, T0xx, specs/<feature>/).

Trigger-graph observation: three skills form a deliberate review triangle — engineering-review (catch-all) delegates test code to test-guard and disclaims git state to commit-workflow; the two performance skills and backend-structure-review carve sub-domains out of the same "review" utterance space. The only unguarded overlaps are backend-structure-review ("when new backend folders or files are added") and pr-context-prep vs engineering-review on "merge-readiness".

Environment-level trigger collision (outside the 10 but affecting them): coderabbit:code-review declares itself "Default code-review skill... for any explicit review request AND autonomously"; /review, code-review:code-review, and superpowers:requesting-code-review also claim review requests. A generic "review this" utterance has at least 5 plausible claimants including engineering-review. NEEDS_MEASUREMENT (routing behavior not observable statically).

speckit-* measured for size only per task scope. .agents speckit copies are full forks, not pointers — unlike the 10 project skills — so speckit rule-drift between .claude and .agents is structurally possible (hook sections already diverge).
